title_zh: 鎮州臨濟慧照禪師語錄
title_en: The Record of Linji (The Zen Teaching of Rinzai)
author_zh: 臨濟義玄 禪師 說 / 門人 三聖慧然 編
author_en: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Linji Yixuan (d. 866), Compiled by Sansheng Huiran

sections.title_en: Sermon: The True Person of No Rank

dialogue.speaker: Linji / 臨濟
dialogue.zh: 師示眾云：「赤肉團上有一無位真人，常從諸人面門出入。未證據者看看！」
dialogue.pinyin: Shī shì zhòng yún: 'Chì ròu tuán shàng yǒu yī wú wèi zhēn rén, cháng cóng zhū rén miàn mén chū rù. Wèi zhèng jù zhě kàn kàn!'

translations.sasaki: The Master instructed the assembly, saying: 'On your lump of red flesh is a True Person of No Rank who is constantly going in and out through your facial gates. Those who have not yet recognized him: look, look!'
translations.cleary: The Master addressed the assembly: 'On this lump of red flesh is a true human of no status, constantly entering and exiting through the gates of your face. Those who have not experienced this, look! Look!'
translations.suzuki: The Master said: 'In this lump of red meat there is a True Man of No Title, always entering and leaving through your senses. Look at him, you who have not yet seen him!'
translations.ai_literal: The Master showed the group, saying: 'Upon the red flesh lump there is a no-rank true person, always entering and leaving through everyone's face gates. Those who haven't verified it: look, look!'

dialogue.speaker: Monk / 僧
dialogue.zh: 時有僧出問：「如何是無位真人？」
dialogue.pinyin: Shí yǒu sēng chū wèn: 'Rúhé shì wú wèi zhēn rén?'

translations.sasaki: Then a monk came forward and asked: 'What is the True Person of No Rank?'
translations.cleary: Then a monk came forward and asked, 'What is the true human of no status?'
translations.suzuki: A monk stepped out and asked: 'What kind of person is the True Man of No Title?'
translations.ai_literal: At that time a monk stepped out and asked: 'What is the no-rank true person?'

dialogue.speaker: Linji / 臨濟
dialogue.zh: 師下禪床，把住云：「道！道！」僧擬議。師託開云：「無位真人是什麼乾屎橛！」便歸方丈。
dialogue.pinyin: Shī xià chánchuáng, bǎzhù yún: 'Dào! Dào!' Sēng nǐyì. Shī tuōkāi yún: 'Wú wèi zhēn rén shì shénme gān shǐ jué!' Biàn guī fāngzhàng.

translations.sasaki: The Master stepped down from the meditation seat, seized the monk, and said: 'Speak! Speak!' The monk hesitated. The Master pushed him away, saying: 'The True Person of No Rank—what a dry shit-stick!' and returned to his quarters.
translations.cleary: The Master got down from the meditation seat, grabbed the monk, and said, 'Speak! Speak!' The monk hesitated. The Master shoved him away and said, 'What kind of dry shit-scraper is the true human of no status!' and went back to his room.
translations.suzuki: The Master descended from his chair, seized the monk by the throat, and cried: 'Speak! Speak!' The monk faltered. Pushing him away, the Master shouted: 'What a worthless dried dirt scraper is your True Man of No Rank!' and returned to his abbot room.
translations.ai_literal: The Master stepped down from the meditation bench, gripped him and said: 'Speak! Speak!' The monk deliberated. The Master pushed him aside and said: 'The true person of no rank—what a dried dung scraper!' Then returned to the abbot's room.

sections.title_en: The Four Classifications (Four Dispositions of Person and Environment)

dialogue.speaker: Linji / 臨濟
dialogue.zh: 師晚參示眾云：「我資化有時奪人不奪境，有時奪境不奪人，有時人境俱奪，有時人境俱不奪。」
dialogue.pinyin: Shī wǎn cān shì zhòng yún: 'Wǒ zī huà yǒu shí duó rén bù duó jìng, yǒu shí duó jìng bù duó rén, yǒu shí rén jìng jù duó, yǒu shí rén jìng jù bù duó.'

translations.sasaki: In the evening sermon the Master said: 'Sometimes I snatch away the person but do not snatch away the environment; sometimes I snatch away the environment but do not snatch away the person; sometimes I snatch away both person and environment; sometimes I snatch away neither person nor environment.'
translations.cleary: The Master gave an evening talk to the group: 'Sometimes I take away the person but not the environment; sometimes I take away the environment but not the person; sometimes I take away both person and environment; sometimes I take away neither person nor environment.'
translations.ai_literal: The Master at evening instructions showed the assembly, saying: 'In my transformative teaching, sometimes I take away the person but do not take away the context; sometimes I take away the context but do not take away the person; sometimes person and context are both taken away; sometimes neither person nor context is taken away.'

dialogue.speaker: Monk / 僧
dialogue.zh: 僧問：「如何是奪人不奪境？」師曰：「煦日發生鋪地錦，嬰兒垂髮白如絲。」
dialogue.pinyin: Sēng wèn: 'Rúhé shì duó rén bù duó jìng?' Shī yuē: 'Xù rì fā shēng pū dì jǐn, yīng'ér chuí fà bái rú sī.'

translations.sasaki: A monk asked: 'What is snatching away the person but not the environment?' The Master said: 'The spring sun brings forth life, paving the earth with brocade; the infant's hair hangs down, white as silk.'
translations.cleary: A monk asked, 'What is taking away the person but not the environment?' The Master said, 'The warm sun bursts forth, carpeting the earth with brocade; an infant's hanging hair is white as silk.'
translations.ai_literal: Monk asked: 'What is taking the person and not the environment?' Master said: 'The warm sun generates growth spreading a brocade over the earth; the infant's drooping hair is white as silk threads.'

dialogue.speaker: Monk / 僧
dialogue.zh: 問：「如何是奪境不奪人？」師曰：「王令已行天下遍，將軍塞外絕煙塵。」
dialogue.pinyin: Wèn: 'Rúhé shì duó jìng bù duó rén?' Shī yuē: 'Wáng lìng yǐ xíng tiān xià biàn, jiāng jūn sài wài jué yān chén.'

translations.sasaki: Asked: 'What is snatching away the environment but not the person?' The Master said: 'The sovereign's command is carried out throughout the realm; beyond the border fortress the general leaves no trace of dust.'
translations.cleary: Asked, 'What is taking away the environment but not the person?' The Master said, 'The king's command has already circulated throughout the land; the general beyond the border cuts off all smoke and dust.'
translations.ai_literal: Asked: 'What is taking the environment and not the person?' Master said: 'The king's decree has already traveled universally through all under heaven; the general beyond the frontier cuts off all smoke and dust.'

dialogue.speaker: Monk / 僧
dialogue.zh: 問：「如何是人境俱奪？」師曰：「并汾絕代，獨處一方。」
dialogue.pinyin: Wèn: 'Rúhé shì rén jìng jù duó?' Shī yuē: 'Bìng Fén jué dài, dú chǔ yī fāng.'

translations.sasaki: Asked: 'What is snatching away both person and environment?' The Master said: 'Bing and Fen are cut off from communication, dwelling alone in isolated lands.'
translations.cleary: Asked, 'What is taking away both person and environment?' The Master said, 'Bing and Fen are completely cut off, occupying their own region in isolation.'
translations.ai_literal: Asked: 'What is taking both person and environment?' Master said: 'Bing and Fen isolated from communication, standing alone in a realm.'

dialogue.speaker: Monk / 僧
dialogue.zh: 問：「如何是人境俱不奪？」師曰：「王登寶殿，野老謳歌。」
dialogue.pinyin: Wèn: 'Rúhé shì rén jìng jù bù duó?' Shī yuē: 'Wáng dēng bǎodiàn, yělǎo ōugē.'

translations.sasaki: Asked: 'What is snatching away neither person nor environment?' The Master said: 'The King ascends the jewel palace; the old peasant in the field breaks into song.'
translations.cleary: Asked, 'What is taking away neither person nor environment?' The Master said, 'The king ascends the jewel throne, rustic elders sing their songs.'
translations.ai_literal: Asked: 'What is taking neither person nor environment?' Master said: 'The King ascends the jewel hall; the rustic old peasant sings folk songs.'
